summary.tldr: Lets survivors receive federal pension benefits even if the relationship started after age 60 or after retirement.
what_it_does: Lets survivors receive pension benefits under several federal plans even when the marriage or conjugal relationship began after age 60 or after retirement.

Changes survivor rules for MPs, former MPs, prime ministers and former prime ministers so the survivor must have been married immediately before death or lived in a conjugal relationship for at least one year before death.
Repeals options in several federal pension laws that let some contributors, judges and MPs reduce their own pensions or allowances, and treats past reduction choices as revoked.
Raises child allowances in the Canadian Forces, Public Service and RCMP plans when there is no eligible survivor, the survivor is dead, or the survivor cannot receive an allowance.

Requires survivors to receive variable benefits or payments from defined contribution accounts, and keeps joint and survivor pension benefits when a member has a spouse or common-law partner at the time payments start or later.
who_it_affects: Prime ministers and former prime ministers
summary.background: The bill amends seven federal pension and retirement laws, plus rules for some private pension plans. The drafters say it removes a limit tied to marriage or cohabitation after age 60 or after retirement.
